- If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast slightly.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or shows recent downward momentum, model often underestimates; increase forecast to align with trend.
- After a sharp price spike, model frequently overshoots in the next few days; apply a 1–2 day lag correction downward.
- When sentiment is mixed or neutral (0.33–0.67), model exhibits mean-reversion bias; adjust forecast toward historical mean of last 5–7 days.
- If model forecast is >10% above recent 7-day average, reduce by 5–10% if sentiment is positive; if negative, increase by 5–10% if sentiment is negative.
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture late-stage momentum; add 1–2% upward adjustment if sentiment is bullish in last 3–5 days.
